items.description: Cross-app references resolve through the published set, iteratively — "App A deploys partial architecture -> Publish aggregated set -> App B uses published set and builds its own -> Publish aggregated set -> App A can deploy its complete set. We can do the same with our migration." A consumer in a deploy repo resolves a provider still in HelmCharts, and HelmCharts resolves a provider that has left, each through the provider's interfaces in the published set. Each draws the same instance → instance Serving edge, with the same id, that HelmCharts' one-process resolution draws today. This run does not push HelmCharts (Ruling Q1), so the test phase proves both directions against a dataset snapshot whose helm-charts envelope is the local HelmCharts render. Verified 2026-09-23: ArgoCDTools aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:628-638 — today resolve_host stops at the hint table after the render (verified 2026-09-23); HelmCharts tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py:476 — the same resolve_host (AST-identical, 2026-09-23).
items.rationale: Both directions were proven on a dataset snapshot whose helm-charts envelope is the local HelmCharts render (HelmCharts e134d28, unpushed per Ruling Q1). Consumers that left HelmCharts resolve the providers still in it through the providers' interfaces and draw the same edges with the same ids; HelmCharts without a departed provider draws that provider's edges, with the same ids, through the published interfaces. The same runs against the live set, which holds none of the interfaces, fail as expected — so the resolution really goes through the published interfaces.
evidence: `argo_migrate.py arch <16 held apps> --dataset snapshot.yaml`: all 16 hold, every check ends `equal — every id matches` (test_r1/arch-gate-snapshot-16-apps.txt)

aac-tools direction: electronics-inventory's render (ArgoCDTools ce5efb9) resolves `postgres-pooler-rw.postgres-pas-prd.svc.cluster.local` to `ss:postgres-pas-prd-postgres-pooler-rw` (edges …-serves-electronics-inventory-…-app/-setup) and `auth.ginbov.nl` to `ss:keycloak-prd-keycloak-keycloak`, instance → instance; its 22 relations equal HelmCharts' published 22

HelmCharts direction: with each provider left out (jenkins, postgres-pas, keycloak, elasticsearch, git-sync, youtrack, telegram-mcp, trello-mcp, homeassistant-mcp) HelmCharts builds and redraws all 23 `drawn by helm-charts` edges, each whole relation dict equal to the snapshot's (jenkins 2, keycloak 7, postgres-pas 6, elasticsearch 3, the rest 1)

Live set (no interfaces): jenkins stops at 'HelmCharts does not build without jenkins-prd' on `jenkins.webathome.org` and `jenkins-mcp.home`; electronics-inventory and infra-statistics stop in the generator on hosts that resolve to no provider (test_r1/arch-gate-live-set-negative.txt)

Source: aac-tools image/gen_architecture.py `resolve_host` + `Dataset.serving_at`; HelmCharts tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py `resolve_host` (AST-identical, checked with ast.dump over every function)

items.area: R2 — the published set stays valid
items.description: The published set stays valid at every step of a migration — "We just have to make sure that we keep the published set in a valid state as we migrate stuff." After the bulk-migration session pushes HelmCharts and `AaC/HelmCharts` publishes the patched producer's artifact, the `AaC/Architecture` collect is green. Owed after that push (Ruling Q1): the run loop does not push HelmCharts, so the test phase does not settle this criterion. Before that, the pre-flip gate holds the line at each move (V12). Verified 2026-09-23: /work/AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/decisions.md:632-644 — D50: the collector publishes nothing while both producers declare an app's ids, until the flip's HelmCharts build clears them.
items.rationale: Settled 2026-09-23 by close-out A1. The HelmCharts push (e134d28, via `~/bulk-migration/hc-push.sh`, tests green) triggered IaC/HelmCharts #6695, which succeeded and deployed no release (every Deploying stage empty). AaC/HelmCharts #277 published the patched producer's artifact, and the `AaC/Architecture` collect #1419 that copied it is green.
evidence: IaC/HelmCharts #6695 SUCCESS; AaC/HelmCharts #277 SUCCESS; AaC/Architecture #1419 SUCCESS, 'Copied 1 artifact from "AaC » HelmCharts" build number 277'

items.description: Nothing has to trigger app A's second pass — "when we hit something like this for a new app, we manage this bootstrapping manually. It's not something we have to account for now." No partial-run flag and no automatic re-run of a consumer is built. In both generators an unresolved host still fails the run: every error goes to stderr and no artifact is written. Verified 2026-09-23: ArgoCDTools aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:986-990; HelmCharts tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py:778-783.
items.rationale: No partial-run flag exists in either generator, and an unresolved host is still fatal in both: every error to stderr, exit 1, no artifact. Seen against real renders on the live set.
evidence: aac-tools image/gen_architecture.py:1052-1056 and HelmCharts tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py:834-839: `errors` → stderr → `N unresolved edge(s); no output written` → SystemExit(1); aac-tools' only flags are --stage/--producer/--repo (:739-751), HelmCharts' none

items.description: HelmCharts is patched, not reworked — "I must assume that it can keep working as is. Honestly, I'd prefer you patch it if you need changes in it. I want to limit the amount of work we do on that repo." HelmCharts keeps its own generator and patches it in place. It keeps building when a provider leaves it, and apps that have left resolve the providers still in it. Verified 2026-09-23: HelmCharts tools/deploy/deploy_cli/release.py:174 — a flipped app's chart_name is None, so the generator skips it.
items.rationale: HelmCharts keeps its own generator, patched in place (+112/−16 in tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py, +503/−1 in its tests); no aac-tools generator was adopted and no other HelmCharts file changed. It builds with a provider left out, and apps that left resolve the providers still in it.
evidence: `git diff --stat 399b281..e134d28` in HelmCharts: only tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py and tests/test_gen_architecture.py
Full render with nothing left out: green, 298 elements / 591 relations, arch-validate ✓

items.description: Every provider publishes each in-cluster Service as an interface element: the existing applicationInterfaces kind, with the host in `stats`. This includes the CNPG pooler Services. Every interface, the in-cluster ones and the existing exposed-host ones, is linked directly to the instances behind its Service and not through the application service. The link is an `Association` from the instance to the interface, the same from ApplicationComponent and SystemSoftware instances (Ruling Q2). An interface links only the containers that serve — never a pod's init containers — and no marker field is added to instance elements (Ruling D2). The artifacts pass arch-validate with no Architecture schema change. Verified 2026-09-23: the published relations.schema.json x-allowedTriples allows Association from both SystemSoftware and ApplicationComponent to ApplicationInterface; ArgoCDTools aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:600-625 (provider index; its backing set includes init containers via w["all"], :614-616), :1113-1116 (pooler Services), :1178-1193 (exposed-host interfaces, Assignment to the service only).
items.rationale: Every Service the render places is published as an `if:` interface at `<svc>.<ns>.svc` (poolers included) and every interface, in-cluster and exposed-host, is linked by an Association from each non-init instance behind it; the existing interface → service Assignment is unchanged; no init container is linked; no schema change; the artifacts validate.
evidence: Full HelmCharts render vs. live set: 53 new elements, all `if:` with `stats.url` ending `.svc`; 174 new relations, all `Association`, ids `rel:<instance hint>-behind-<interface hint>`

Jenkins in the snapshot: `if:jenkins-jenkins-prd-svc` (jenkins.jenkins-prd.svc) links only `ss:…-jenkins-jenkins`, not `ss:…-install-homelab-ca`; `if:jenkins-mcp-jenkins-prd-svc` links the auth (SystemSoftware) and filter (ApplicationComponent) instances — both source types validate
`arch-validate` (live service): helm-charts.yaml full render ✓; aac-tools artifacts for jenkins, postgres-pas, keycloak, elasticsearch ✓ (Ansible scripts/arch-validate.py)
Mutations: linking init containers breaks 6 aac-tools tests and a HelmCharts test (test_r1/generator-mutations.txt)

items.area: D1 — the two generators in lockstep
items.description: For the same Service, the aac-tools generator and HelmCharts' generator emit the same interface elements (same ids, every field equal) and the same relations. A moved provider therefore shows no field difference at handover.
items.rationale: The two generators emit the same elements and relations for the same Service: the whole surface is AST-identical, and 16 apps' aac-tools renders equal HelmCharts' render field for field.

items.area: D1 — same providers, same edge ids
items.description: Resolution through the published set picks exactly the providers that in-process resolution picks: the capability's realizers, and the containers a wire's `providers` names. No init container becomes a provider; the live case is jenkins' install-homelab-ca init container, which realizes cap:continuous-integration. Cross-app Serving edges stay instance → instance and keep their ids. Verified 2026-09-23: ArgoCDTools aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:1393, :1464, :1567 — in-process resolution drops init containers.
items.rationale: Resolution through the published set keeps exactly the providers in-process resolution keeps, and cross-app Serving edges stay instance → instance with unchanged ids. Jenkins' init container is not a provider.
evidence: jenkins: HelmCharts without jenkins draws `rel:jenkins-prd-jenkins-jenkins-serves-infra-statistics-…-continuous-integration` (source the `jenkins` container, not `install-homelab-ca`) and `…-jenkins-mcp-filter-serves-intercom-…-mcp`, both whole-dict equal to the snapshot's (gate on jenkins ✓)

items.area: Handover check — whose edges are whose
items.description: An edge drawn by the consumer's producer, meaning a Serving edge into a consumer outside the app, is not reported as the app's loss. It is listed under that consumer's producer. Keycloak's 21 bare-UUID relations are IoTSupport's `keycloak —Serving→ <IoT device>` edges and are classified that way. Verified 2026-09-23: ArgoCDTools aac-tools/checks/handover_equality.py:164-181 — every relation with one endpoint in the app is claimed; /work/scratch/IoTSupport backend/tools/gen-architecture.py:356-364 — IoTSupport mints the rel:<uuid5> ids.
items.rationale: A Serving edge drawn by a consumer outside the app is listed under that consumer's producer and is not the app's loss. Keycloak's 21 bare-UUID relations are classified as IoTSupport's.
evidence: keycloak check on the snapshot: `drawn by iotsupport-app:` ×21 bare-UUID `rel:<uuid>` ids and `drawn by helm-charts:` ×7; ends `equal`; gate line `edges other producers draw: iotsupport-app 21` (test_r1/arch-gate-snapshot-16-apps.txt)
Across the 16: 23 helm-charts-drawn edges, 35 under `iotsupport-app`, 1 under `youtrack-mcp-server`; none of them contains `published but not generated`

items.area: Arch gate — both halves of a move
items.description: Before an app flips, `argo_migrate.py arch` proves both halves of the move. The app's new producer drops no id the published set carries for it. HelmCharts' patched generator, rendering every release except the app's against the same dataset snapshot with nothing overlaid, builds green and still draws every edge from the app to a consumer that stays in HelmCharts, with the same id. The gate runs against a snapshot file as well as the live set; the test phase proves it on a snapshot whose helm-charts envelope is the local HelmCharts render. Verified 2026-09-23: HelmCharts tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py:521, :584 (subset render), :343-345 (default DockerImages overlay); Ansible support/argo-migrate/argo_migrate.py:735-736 (cmd_arch passes no --dataset); ArgoCDTools aac-tools/checks/handover_equality.py:233 (the check takes --dataset).
items.rationale: `argo_migrate.py arch` proves both halves against one snapshot with nothing overlaid, from a file (`--dataset`) as well as the live URL. It stops on a lost or redrawn edge and on a HelmCharts that cannot build without the app; it passes on the snapshot.
evidence: 16 held apps on the snapshot: all hold, HelmCharts builds green without each and draws all 23 helm-charts-drawn edges (test_r1/arch-gate-snapshot-16-apps.txt)
Mutated snapshots: an extra field on the published edge → `helm-charts would redraw …`; the edge under another id → `helm-charts would no longer draw …` (test_r1/gate-mutations.txt B, C)
Live set: jenkins → `HelmCharts does not build without jenkins-prd:` with the two unresolved edges (test_r1/arch-gate-live-set-negative.txt)

Side effects held to scratch: harness redirected HOME/deploy-repo location; ~/bulk-migration/state/jenkins-prd.json untouched (mtime 13:03). HelmCharts' gitignored docs/architecture/helm-charts.yaml is overwritten by each run, as the done-record says

Every id loss attributable to cross-app resolution is gone. Any app that still stops is named with its cause, and no such cause is cross-app resolution.
